Icelandic

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Norse fé, from Proto-Germanic *fehu, from Proto-Indo-European *péḱu (“livestock, domestic animals”). Cognate with English fee.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fjɛː/
  • Rhymes: -ɛː

Noun

[edit]

fé n (genitive singular fjár or (proscribed) fjárs or fés, nominative plural (archaic/obsolete) fé)

  1. livestock; cattle, chiefly sheep
  2. assets
  3. money
  4. fehu; the first letter of the runic futhark alphabet

Usage notes

[edit]
  • Now singular only, this noun had plural forms in Old Icelandic.
  • The proscribed forms fjárs and fés sometimes appear, see Ritmálssafn. Compare to the proscribed genitive singular form föðurs of the r-stem faðir or to the other similar neuters ending in -é, hné and tré.

Declension

[edit]

indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative fé féð fé1 fén1
accusative fé féð fé1 fén1
dative fé fénu fjám1 fjánum1
genitive fjár, fjárs2, fés2 fjárins, fjársins2, fésins2 fjá1 fjánna1

1Archaic/obsolete.
2Proscribed.

Irish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Irish fo, from *wo, from Proto-Celtic *uɸo, from Proto-Indo-European *upo. Compare Ancient Greek ὑπό (hupó), Middle Welsh go.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fʲeː/

Preposition

[edit]

fé (plus dative, triggers lenition)

  1. Munster form of faoi (“under; about, concerning”)

Related terms

[edit]
  • faoi (standard and Connacht form)

Old Norse

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Germanic *fehu (“livestock, wealth”), from Proto-Indo-European *péḱu.

Noun

[edit]

fé n (genitive fjár)

  1. cattle; livestock, (especially sheep)
  2. property, money

Declension

[edit]
Declension of fé (strong u-stem)
masculine singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative fé féit fé féin
accusative fé féit fé féin
dative fé fénu féum, fjám, fjóm fjánum, fjónum
genitive féar, fjár féarins, fjárins féa, fjá féanna, fjánna

The gen. sg./pl. & dat. pl. forms come from the West Norse change -éa- > -já-. Compare sjá, whereas East N. séa.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • eyrir (money)
  • fær (sheep)
  • sauðr (sheep)

Portuguese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • fè (obsolete)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese fe, fee, from Latin fidem, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰidʰ-, zero-grade of *bʰeydʰ- (“to command, to persuade, to trust”). Compare Fala and Galician fe.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfɛ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈfɛ/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛ
  • Hyphenation: fé

Noun

[edit]

fé f (plural fés)

  1. faith
  2. belief

Derived terms

[edit]
  • a fé move montanhas
  • auto da fé
  • boa-fé
  • fé púnica
  • má-fé
  • salto de fé

Related terms

[edit]
  • fidelidade
  • fiel

Descendants

[edit]
  • ⇒ Konkani: फेभावार्थ (phebhāvārtha)
